research_question: Can expensive offline policy improvement reduce no-miss failures while leaving the deployed CPU actor and native safety path unchanged?

deployment_contract.online_model_change: actor weights only; architecture and parameter count are unchanged

success_only_elite_distillation.update: elite negative log likelihood plus behavior-policy KL; encoder, GRU, and critic frozen
success_only_elite_distillation.decision: reject; success-only behavior cloning does not identify which sampled actions caused success

outcome_conditioned_actor_update.advantages: episode utilities centered and standardized across the frozen behavior-policy dataset
outcome_conditioned_actor_update.objective: clipped behavior-policy importance ratio plus behavior-to-student KL
outcome_conditioned_actor_update.policy_credit: native mid-transaction overrides and all bomb actions excluded; movement actions remain attributable

selection_objective_audit.previous_order: all clears, then no-miss clears, then return LCB
selection_objective_audit.corrected_order: no-miss clears, then all clears, then return LCB
selection_objective_audit.reason: the declared deployment objective is perfect completion, so a clear with a miss cannot outrank a no-miss clear

outcome_conditioned_actor_update.decision: provisionally accept for the next curriculum phase; improvement is small and based on eight held-out attempts

online_latency_audit.interpretation: the deployed decision path is small enough for real-time use on one CPU thread, and the transactional harness additionally pauses the emulator during inference

conclusion: The online/offline separation is supported at the systems level and receives preliminary gameplay support. Success-only distillation and additional online PPO are rejected on held-out data. A conservative positive-and-negative outcome update improves held-out no-miss clears from 6/8 to 7/8 and removes two observed deaths without changing online architecture, while p99 decision latency remains 1.530 ms. This is not evidence of full-stage or cross-game mastery; the next test must move the curriculum start earlier and retain untouched evaluation seeds.
